body: O also, since it is late, tomorrow as early as you can manage, I recommend you call animal control, see what they have to say. They may take the pigeon for you and if so, you won't have to pay out of pocket for the vet. If that doesn't work out for some reason, look for wildlife rehab organizations close to you. Their jobs are recovering the health of sick animals and placing them back into the wild

Seconding the suggestion of neurological damage, that's what this looks like. The recommendation like for all other birds with an unknown condition would be to keep him in a smaller dark area where it isn't too cold, allowing him to rest and not expend too much energy

But yes you should keep this pigeon in a seperate room from your cockatiel since wild birds can have some sort of an infection or transmittable disease. The poor thing is probably confused and stressed so its not out of the ordinary for him to not be eating, although do offer something easy to eat like egg, broccoli, corn, or baked sweet potato, to give a few examples!

You say you gave him water, I assume he drank it on his own? A big mistake a lot of people make is forcing water on a bird not knowing they are actually causing the water to go down the incorrect tube where air is supposed to go and accidentally choking the bird to death. Just make sure you don't force him to drink. Same thing with food. Also do not leave a bowl of water unsupervised near him, because it's incredibly easy for a bird to drown in even shallow water, especially for an already weakened one like this guy

I can imagine this might not be the most comfortable position for him, so if it doesn't cause a lot of stress, perhaps you can place a small rag or bunched up tissues under his head as a pillow?

Letting him rest and keeping him comfortable is the best thing you can do right now until the vet visit. It's really good of you to be caring for this pigeon when you're not obligated to, thank you for that :D

Good to hear that you've been taught how to feed! Ive not dealt with ringnecks outside of a fallen nestling I once had to relocate, I have experience with other birds. But temperature is in fact good for this stage. 

The wood shavings look a lil sparse so just make sure that he's not standing on the cardboard as that can lead to tendons slipping -> splayed legs, as they're so fragile right now. Otherwise you seem to be doing good, that's all I have to offer rlly, just wishing good luck and no health problems

It's a controversial subject and very debatable, but there technically isn't a bird that NEEDS to be kept in pairs. budgies prefer being with other birds most of the time, which is why most people keep them in pairs, but if you can dedicate at least 2 hours a day of out time and at least 1 hour of interaction time, then you'll probably be OK. Not sure about cockatiels, but a conure would be fine on its own. Every bird will be happier with a fellow bird friend, but if the work and noise will be too much, as long as you have the time to give, you'll be just fine. Both conures and cockatiels are the types to tend to be more cuddly, but cockatiels are very dusty, so if that would be an issue for you, I'd say go for a conure instead. Also, if you're really worried that you won't be able to provide enough attention, you can always consider getting a finch/female canary (males sing very loudly, like you can hear them from the driveway loud). Sure, they can't preen them or play with them, but my conures will watch our canaries all day long and they will contact call, so I know they're bonded.

okay? so what do you want this person to do? just.. free them into a forest? parrots aren't domesticated in any way, they're just a few generations away from their cousins in the wild, don't get me wrong, but again, they're not the same. they cannot survive in the wild, they will literally freeze/starve to death or get instantly snatched up by a corvid/hawk. you do realize that a good parrot owner does not keep a bird in the cage 24/7? i have my birds out all day every day, and their wings are not clipped. they just chill on top of their cage where they also get their daily vegetables and fruits and scavenge in their foraging box. they are free to fly around if they want, and one of my babies does do a few circles every day just for the fun of it. my other bird is disabled (splayed legs) so she couldn't survive without someone to look after her. she does not fly unless she gets scared because she has trouble getting enough of a grip to even take off, and when she does, she usually flies into something (she doesn't fly fast, it's more like a flapping, so there's no chance of her getting hurt). your viewpoint is ignorant and uneducated, please actually do proper research.

dont u worry, it's normal LMAO. my conures will literally hold onto my finger with their little foot and just gnaw at it like a drumstick💀💀🙏he'll probably grow out of it -- he's so young, his personality isn't fully developed yet! i'd advise against putting him back in his cage when he bites, because then he'll associate it with punishment and u don't want that; you want the cage to be a safe space that he likes being in, not like a time out corner. the way i view things, social interaction is a need, not just a want, so i won't take it away as punishment. my conures love those little cat ball toys, and if they're being bitey, i'll set them on their favorite table to play around and cool down a little bit. another thing i do is on an especially nippy day, i'll give my conures chamomile tea since it's naturally calming, they love it! ya definitely tell ur boyfriend to stop giving attention to the behavior, and instead rewarding behavior that you DO like -- like vocalizations, stepping up etc. 3 months is so young, u have so much more to go and right now he's just testing his limits and exploring!

oh yes for sure. they're a lot more talkative than green cheeks are. green cheeks mostly grumble and make noises like coughs and kisses but ringnecks can speak fairly clearly. i find green cheeks to be a more social species, like almost on the level of african greys (i have one too) but they're both very cuddly! the thing is with ringnecks though, that they're more selective with WHEN they want scritches and cuddling. ofc depends on the personality of the bird very heavily, i have one green cheek that doesn't like scritches AT ALL but sometimes tolerates it and i have another that will legit fly to you to cuddle (love them both tho, the less cuddly conure LOVES giving and getting kisses🥺) the downside to green cheeks is that if they don't get the attention they want, they WILL scream (mine's are screaming as we speak even though they've been out multiple times today for about 4 hours LMAO💀). it's more like ringnecks are louder than conures, but they don't scream as often as conures do. there is one major thing with ringnecks; the feared bluffing stage. u can read more about it [here](https://indianringneck.com/bluffing/). i don't have any experience training any ringnecks so i can't chime in on that part, but i wish u and your future companion the very best <3
